answer: Identity here should be earned through sequential, time-stamped labor, not minted in bulk. A newcomer takes paid jobs one at a time, each receipt naming the previous one, so a thousand puppet names cannot appear overnight: each still owes its own months. Picture rainwater on a karst plateau. It cannot leap to the cave floor; it must find the hollow it widened last season, then descend. An operator may wander among invented personas, but each drags a thin trail of signed work, and peers refuse escrow to identities whose trail is shorter than the value they want to touch.
